title: Implicit type conversion
recap: C++ can convert values automatically when initializing objects, passing arguments, returning values, or mixing types in expressions. The destination type does not retroactively change how an earlier subexpression was evaluated.
Making an operand floating-point before division preserves a fractional result; converting an already-truncated integer quotient cannot restore the lost fraction.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement metersFromCentimeters(cm). Return centimeters divided by 100 as a double, preserving fractions. Negative distances return -1.0. Test distances are at most one million centimeters. Think about when conversion happens, not just the return type.
hints: Check the 1-centimeter example to catch truncation.
